target_customer: Indian state judiciaries and High Courts (courts, judges, court staff), funded by governments and philanthropy
problem: Indian courts face huge backlogs and a shortage of stenographers; clerical work such as typing depositions slows every case.
business_model: Nonprofit-style justice technology provided to courts, funded by grants and philanthropic capital; YC listing shows it as a company
product_category: Legal tech: court speech-to-text transcription and case workflow

competitors.name: Supreme Court of India in-house AI transcription
competitors.what: Automated near-real-time transcription of Constitution Bench hearings
competitors.traction_then: Began February 2023 for constitutional matters only

competitors.name: SUVAS
competitors.what: Judicial document translation tool, translation rather than transcription

technical_complexity.rationale: Speech-to-text for Indian accents, languages and legal terms, deployed in noisy courtrooms and integrated into court workflows; generative AI made it feasible for a small team in 2023.

defensibility.rationale: State High Court mandates (Kerala from 1 November 2025) and integration into court procedure create strong lock-in once adopted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Government bodies built limited transcription for the apex court but Adalat spread across district courts in several states.

market_need_then: Severe stenographer shortage and case backlogs in lower courts; the founder says generative AI maturity in summer 2023 made the idea feasible.

branding.domain_note: Uses adalat.ai (AI domain), with adalat.ai also appearing in press as Adalat.ai.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven justice access tone in interviews

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by ThePrint, YourStory, Bar and Bench, Stanford GSB case study and SSIR; this is press about the work more than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong credibility in Indian courts and press, but sources describe impact not the brand itself. Adalat is a Hindi and Urdu word for court (general knowledge, not from a cited source).

outcome_analysis: Adalat AI was founded in 2023 after generative AI made accurate court transcription practical, and it spread to roughly a quarter of India's courtrooms across 11 states by late 2026, helped by a Kerala High Court mandate. It is funded by grants and philanthropy, not venture rounds, so growth rests on government adoption rather than commercial sales.
notes: Funding is grant based. CB Insights lists about 340K USD total (Elevate Prize, MIT Solve, Fast Forward, 100x Impact Accelerator), Dealroom a 25K grant, Inc42 an undisclosed 2024 grant; these are aggregator figures and conflict, so no round is recorded. SSIR names MIT Solve, Mulago Rainer Arnhold Fellowship, Echoing Green, Fast Forward and The/Nudge Institute as supporters, without amounts. Deployment counts conflict (2,500, 3,000, 4,000 courtrooms). No layoffs, shutdown or criticism found.
